title: Brain regions involved in object-location memory in healthy adults: A systematic review and activation likelihood estimation meta-analysis of task-based fMRI
title_zh: 健康成年人中物体位置记忆相关的脑区：系统综述与激活可能性估计元分析
abstract: The ability to remember where objects are located is a fundamental cognitive function particularly vulnerable to aging and neurodegenerative disease. Previous functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) research has combined object-location memory (OLM) with broader spatial memory and navigation tasks, resulting in inconsistent findings. This systematic review and coordinate-based activation likelihood estimation (ALE) meta-analysis isolated OLM to characterize brain regions engaged during encoding and retrieval in healthy adults, with additional exploratory analyses of age effects. Searches of PubMed, PsycInfo, and the Cochrane Library identified 21 eligible task-based fMRI studies comprising 622 participants. Twelve studies contributed to an encoding ALE, which identified significant spatial convergence in left and right ventral occipitotemporal regions encompassing the fusiform and parahippocampal gyri. The left cluster was supported by 8 of 12 experiments, survived all leave-one-experiment-out iterations, and was recovered by an independent coordinate-based framework, supporting a robust ventral occipitotemporal substrate for OLM encoding. An OLM retrieval ALE including four studies yielded no significant convergence, most likely reflecting the limited number of eligible studies. Retrieval findings were therefore synthesized narratively. These studies most frequently implicated the hippocampus and precuneus, suggesting a different regional pattern from encoding, although the phases were not statistically compared. Only three studies directly compared age groups, suggesting altered hippocampal engagement during retrieval in older adults. By isolating OLM from broader spatial-memory constructs, this review identifies a robust encoding substrate while highlighting current research gaps that need to be addressed. This review was preregistered on PROSPERO (CRD420251023695).
abstract_zh: 能够记住物体的位置是一种基本的认知功能，特别容易受衰老和神经退行性疾病的影响。以往的功能性磁共振成像（fMRI）研究将物体位置记忆（OLM）与更广泛的空间记忆和导航任务结合，导致了结果不一致。本系统综述和基于坐标的激活可能性估计（ALE）元分析旨在单独分析物体位置记忆，以刻画健康成年人在编码和检索过程中激活的脑区，并额外进行了年龄效应的探索性分析。通过PubMed、PsycInfo和Cochrane Library的检索，筛选出21项符合条件的基于任务的fMRI研究，共包含622名参与者。其中12项研究参与了编码的ALE分析，结果在左侧和右侧腹侧顶叶区域（包括颞叶和海马旁回）表现出显著的空间收敛。左侧簇由8项实验支持，经全部“删除一项实验”迭代后存活，且由独立的基于坐标的框架回收，这支持了腹侧顶叶在物体位置记忆编码中具有稳健的亚基。包含4项研究的物体位置记忆检索ALE分析未发现显著收敛，这最可能反映了符合条件研究的有限数量。因此，检索结果采用了叙述性综合。这些研究最频繁地涉及海马体和旁叶，表明与编码相比存在不同的区域模式，尽管各相位未进行统计比较。仅有3项研究直接比较了年龄组，这提示老年人检索时海马体参与度可能发生改变。通过将物体位置记忆与更广泛的空间记忆构象隔离开来，本综述确定了一个稳健的编码亚基，同时也突出了目前需要解决的研究空白。本综述在PROSPERO（CRD420251023695）上预先注册。
